claim: A November 2021 Vibely/Ian Borthwick study of 150 content creators (45.3% with 100k-500k followers, 0.7% with 5M+) found that 90% had experienced burnout and 71% said it made them consider quitting content production altogether.
stance_target: prevalence of self-reported creator burnout and quit consideration - the origin of the recirculated '90% of creators' figure
scope_conditions: SELF-SELECTED VENDOR SURVEY of n=150 using mixed qualitative methods, recruited by a startup (Vibely) simultaneously building and marketing an anti-burnout product - direct commercial conflict of interest, acknowledged even by the reporting outlet ('that advice isn't totally objective'). Sample skews toward mid-to-large established creators (100k-500k followers most common), not the long tail. No country, sampling frame, or confidence interval stated. Measures quit CONSIDERATION among still-active creators, not observed exit; cannot sample anyone who already quit. The 71% figure is nearly double BDB's 37% (n=1,000, 2025) four years later - the gap is more plausibly explained by sample size, follower-tier selection, and pandemic-era timing than by a real change in quit intention over time, so the two figures should not be treated as a comparable trend.
quoted_support: "A whopping 90% of creators told Vibely they had experienced burnout, and 71% said it had made them consider quitting content production altogether."

claim: Among the 150 surveyed creators, top burnout stressors were algorithm/platform changes (65%), need to make a living from content (59%), constant-production 'hamster wheel effect' (51%), follower-count anxiety (51%), harassment/bullying (42%), impostor syndrome (29%), and backlash risk (19%).
stance_target: documented reasons creators give for burnout/quit consideration
scope_conditions: Same n=150 self-selected, vendor-conflicted sample as the headline 90%/71% figures; not comparable across studies without adjusting for follower-tier skew and method.
quoted_support: "A full 65% of respondents said that one of their top stressors is changes to platforms' algorithms... 59% of creators also cited the need to make a living off content as a top stressor."
